stance.label: US pullback deepens, Taiwan in a bear market; stick to the plan

headline: US stocks fall a sixth day, S&P 500 −2%; Anthropic debut fails to lift AI; Taiwan night futures −500
summary: US stocks are still in a pullback, not a turn down, but AI selling has not found a floor. The S&P 500 fell 2% to 2.3% under its 200-day line, with only 1 systemic light on; the Nasdaq flipped from gains to losses. Taiwan opens under pressure today; watch whether the short-sale curbs slow foreign selling. Keep regular investing on plan.

watch.label: S&P 500 200-day line
watch.note: Closed 7,175.83 on 11/19, 2.3% below for 3 days; weak only after 5 closes with a flat line

watch.label: QQQ fourth tier (−20% from high)

overview.lead: This is an AI confidence problem, not an economic one: Anthropic's strong debut could not hold up tech, and the market fell a sixth day.
points: S&P 500 fell 2%, its 6th straight loss.
The Dow fell 1,101 points to 49,097.
The Nasdaq was up 2.1% at one point and closed down 2.25%.
Losers swamped winners: about 4.4 decliners per advancer on the NYSE.
Nvidia (NVDA) fell a 6th day; AMD (AMD) fell 7.7%.

focus.lead: QQQ hit its third tier last night, the only new change among the nine; the two Taiwan funds' NAVs now reflect the 11/19 plunge, down close to 40% from highs.
points: QQQ closed 645.04, −15.1% from its high, hitting the third tier.
QQQ's next tier is 607.73, 5.8% away.
SPY's second tier at 701.18 is only 2.1% away, the closest of the nine.
Allianz Taiwan Technology (TW000T3604Y3) NAV fell 7.9% on 11/19, −38.4% from its high, the deepest of the nine.
Cathay Taiwan High Dividend (TW000T3786A8) NAV fell 6.6% on 11/19, −34.4% from its high.
Four overseas funds' NAVs run only to 11/18 and miss last night's US drop.

position.lead: QQQ hit its third tier; under the framework that brings it to 45% of reserved cash. The other eight hit no new tier.
points: QQQ fourth tier 607.73, 5.8% away.
SPY second tier 701.18, 2.1% away.
0050 fifth tier 81.55, 9.6% away.
AB American Growth (LU0683600562) second tier 85.08, 4.1% away (11/18 NAV).
AB International Technology (LU0060230025) fifth tier 1,218.74, 7.6% away (11/18 NAV).
Allianz Taiwan Technology and Cathay Taiwan High Dividend have used every tier; further drops trigger nothing new.

macro.lead: Economic data is still solid; rate hikes are what weigh on stocks. Markets all but expect a 25 bp December hike, and the 10-year stays above 5%.
points: CME FedWatch puts a 25 bp December hike at 96.4%.
10-year Treasury yield 5.04%, 2-year 4.76%.
Initial jobless claims 203K (week of 11/14); jobs have not turned.
High-yield spread 3.47% (11/18), far from the 5% alarm line.
Next week's PCE is expected to show core inflation of 3.2%, still above target.

sentiment.lead: US fear is rising but not extreme: the VIX curve is inverted, and 2 bottoming signals are on.
points: The VIX jumped to 28.44, in the top 99% of the past year.
The VIX curve is inverted: the 9-day sits above the 3-month, so short-term hedging demand is surging.
CNN Fear & Greed is 18.7, extreme fear.
S&P 500 RSI is 31, close to oversold but not there yet.
Only 5 of 11 sectors are above their 200-day lines.

sectors.lead: Everything closed lower, with AI infrastructure hit hardest; security software and strong earners were rare exceptions.
points: The semiconductor ETF (SMH) fell 2.6% and is down nearly 20% in a month.
Communication and consumer discretionary each fell nearly 3% as big platforms were sold together.
CoreWeave (CRWV) fell 6.1%; Nebius (NBIS) fell 9.4%.
Palo Alto (PANW) raised its 2027 revenue outlook and rose 6.4%.
After hours, Intuit (INTU) fell 13% on a weak forecast.

taiwan.lead: Taiwan opens into last night's US sell-off, with night futures already down 500 points; short-sale curbs start today, so watch whether foreign selling eases.
points: Taiex night futures fell 500 points to 38,107.
TSMC ADR (TSM) fell 2.9%, at a 10.4% premium.
ASE ADR (ASX) fell 6.2%; UMC ADR (UMC) fell 4%.
Foreigners have sold 4 days in a row, about NT$180.3B this week.
Foreign net short Taiex futures stay high at 99,219 contracts.
NT$ at 32.91 on 11/18; the sharp-depreciation light is not on.

watch.lead: Today, watch whether Taiwan's slide below the bear line steadies and foreigners pull back; in the US, watch whether Nvidia stops falling.
points: FSC short-sale curbs start today: stocks closing down 3.5% or more cannot be shorted below the prior close the next day.
The Taiex must get back above 39,858 to leave bear territory.
Two more S&P 500 closes under the 200-day line make 5; with the line still rising, that alone does not flag weakness.
Next week's US PCE is key to the size of the December hike.
US markets close for Thanksgiving on 11/26.

regime.lead: By the rules, US stocks are still a pullback in an uptrend; Taiwan is a bear with rising risk, one light from being called a downtrend.
points: Trend: the S&P 500 is 2.3% under its 200-day line, below it 3 days, and the line still rises.
Systemic lights: only 1 on in the US (below the 200-day line); credit, the economy and financial conditions are fine.
Closest to turning on is credit: the high-yield spread is 3.47%, still well short of 5%.
Bottoming signals: 2 on in the US (VIX curve inverted, extreme fear); the VIX is not yet at the panic line.
History: of 97 S&P 500 drops to this level, 19 went past −20%.
Of 57 drops this fast, 8 went past −20%; most stopped near −10%.
Taiwan: all 9 drops to this level went past −20%, but the 12-month median was +18.8%.
What flips the call: 5 S&P 500 closes under 7,348 with a flat line means weak.
3+ lights on means a possible turn down; below 6,255 is a bear market.

news.read: Nvidia is a top holding of QQQ and both AB US funds; its slide pushed QQQ to its third tier.

news.title: CME FedWatch: 96.4% odds of a 25 bp December hike; next week's PCE seen at 3.2% core
news.read: A hike is nearly certain, weighing on growth valuations and keeping the dollar strong and the NT$ weak.

news.title: Walmart (WMT) Q3 revenue of $188.84B beat and it raised full-year sales guidance, yet the stock fell about 1%
news.read: US consumers have not cracked; the economy supports the pullback-not-downturn call.

news.title: Intuit (INTU) guided next-quarter EPS to $3.17–3.22, below forecasts, and fell 13% after hours
news.read: Software outlooks are softening too, another weight on tech at the next open.

news.title: FSC curbs: from 11/20, stocks closing down 3.5% or more cannot be shorted below the prior close the next day
news.read: Curbs can slow the chase lower but do not change foreign selling; watch whether pressure eases today.
